clue.text: Dance in revolutionary period is futile

indicators.note: in puts the dance inside the turned-round period
revolutionary means turning round, so the period is read backwards

parts.note: an eon is a vast period of time
to hop is to dance, as at a hop

explanation.surface: A judgement that dancing during a revolution is a waste of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like politics but turns the period round; 'in' then sets the dance inside it. 'No-hope' is a hyphenated adjective, as in a no-hope candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hope attempt is a doomed, pointless one, so the hyphenated adjective is a synonym for futile.

clue.text: Wanting Mark to underpin articulated joint

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece that underpins sits below the other
articulated means spoken, so the joint is taken by its sound, silent K and all

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
a ding is a small dent or mark on a surface

explanation.surface: An instruction about a mark placed beneath a jointed part, as if in engineering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articulated' looks like the jointed part's description but says KNEE is spoken: NEE. 'to underpin' puts DING below it in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanting in the sense of lacking or requiring something is a synonym of the participle needing.

clue.text: Problem couple

definitions.meaning: a snag or difficulty, as in a technical glitch
as a verb, to hook up or attach, as a trailer to a car

explanation.surface: A troubled pair, or a hitch in a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both a snag and to attach one thing to another, as with a tow bar.

clue.text: Official's totally right to drop first point

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is just the official

indicators.note: the right letter drops back ahead of the first compass point in the word for totally

parts.note: perfect can mean utter or total, as in a perfect stranger

explanation.surface: Someone claims an official is completely correct to abandon an opening argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, E: R in PERFECT moves to stand before the first E. 'Official's' reads as possessive but means 'Official is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefect is an official, historically a Roman magistrate and now a senior pupil or French administrator.

clue.text: Picture of legendary king

definitions.meaning: a film; a 1981 comedy starring Dudley Moore
the king of Camelot and the Round Table

explanation.surface: A portrait of a mythical monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' suggests a painting but means a film here.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruler of Camelot is the mythical British monarch, and a 1981 movie shares his name.

clue.text: Sovereign's upset amateur soldiers

definitions.note: used adjectivally, belonging to a monarch

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in this down light the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: lay means non-professional, as a lay preacher
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A monarch is dismayed by part-time troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an emotion but turns LAYOR upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Things of a king or queen are regal, so the adjective substitutes for a possessive meaning of the monarch.

clue.text: Area of land holds landscape features

parts.note: HA is the abbreviation for hectare, a metric area of land
has means holds or possesses

explanation.surface: A plot of ground contains various scenic elements.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch and wall that bounds a park without blocking the view, a feature of English country estates.
explanation.definitionFit: These sunken boundary ditches are designed elements in landscaped gardens, so they are examples of landscape features.

clue.text: Work and other things arising to be behind schedule

parts.note: to run is to work or operate, as a machine runs

indicators.note: arising means coming up, so in this down light the Latin phrase is read upwards

parts.note: et al, Latin et alia, means and other things

explanation.surface: Jobs and sundry extras keep cropping up, leaving one behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns ETAL upwards to LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trains and meetings that fail to keep to time are behind schedule, the meaning of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: One's perception of folk legends we translated

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Insight gained from rendering traditional myths into another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges FOLK LEGENDS WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness of one's own nature and character is how one perceives oneself, the sense of the compound.

clue.text: This is the result of prang? Not half!

definitions.text: This is the result of prang? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means one half is left out, here the first four of eight letters

parts.note: prang is British slang for a car crash, an accident

explanation.surface: Someone surveys a crash damage and exclaims emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'absolutely', but here it cuts the first half from ACCIDENT. The whole clue also defines: a dent is what a prang leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor crash typically leaves a hollow in bodywork, so a dent is the result of a bump.

clue.text: The Works, say, stocks pretty light

indicators.note: stocks means holds within, so the example abbreviation contains the rest

parts.note: say, as in for example, gives EG
pretty can mean very, as in pretty good
thin means light or flimsy, as thin fabric

explanation.surface: The Works is a British discount bookshop chain, which here sells attractive lamps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Works' poses as the shop name but means the whole lot; 'stocks' puts VERYTHIN inside EG.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole works is an idiom for all of it, the entire set.

clue.text: Chilli cheeseburger contains exotic item

indicators.note: contains says the answer is held within the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A spicy burger hides an unusual ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' finds the letters across chilLI CHEEseburger.
explanation.definitionFit: The lychee, also spelt lichee, is a Chinese fruit, so it is an exotic item of produce.

clue.text: Actor covers revolutionary singer

parts.note: films can mean thin covering layers, as in films of dust

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word for singer is read backwards

parts.note: a rat is an informer, someone who sings to the police

explanation.surface: A performer records cover versions of songs by a rebel musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' looks musical but is a squealer, RAT; 'revolutionary' turns it into TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated performer in movies is an actor, so this is an example of the definition.

clue.text: European worker probes row about German growth

indicators.note: probes means pushes into, so the worker goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a line is a row, as a line of people; about here only joins it to the German letter
the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

explanation.surface: A European labourer investigates a dispute involving a German plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a LINE; ANT goes into GLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is sweet briar, a wild rose, so it is a plant, a kind of growth.

clue.text: Cockney's shock broadcast

indicators.note: a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, traditionally drops the initial aitch

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it

explanation.surface: An East Londoner is startled by something on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' looks like a fright but is a mop of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a programme is to transmit it, so the verb is a synonym for broadcast.

clue.text: Sentence in biography

definitions.meaning: a prison term for the rest of one's days
a written account of someone's days

explanation.surface: A judge's ruling written up in a memoir.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a whole-of-days prison term and a written account of a person's history.

clue.text: Evil state

definitions.meaning: as a noun, harm or misfortune
.... is the abbreviation for the US state of Illinois

explanation.surface: A wicked country.
explanation.definitionFit: An ill is a harm, and the same letters abbreviate Illinois, a US state.

clue.text: Cross and brazen after losing series of battles?

indicators.note: after losing means once something is taken away, so the war goes from the word for brazen

parts.note: forward means bold or presumptuous
a war is a series of battles

explanation.surface: Someone angry and shameless after defeat in a military campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ford a river is to cross it at a shallow place, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Getting nothing out of establishing sponsorship

indicators.note: out of means taken from, so the zero letter comes away

parts.note: founding means establishing, as founding a company
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A start-up gets no money from setting up a sponsorship deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing' gives O, a zero shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Money provided by a backer is financial support, so sponsorship is a synonym for it.

clue.text: Damp lawns turned into quagmire

indicators.note: turned means altered or reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wet grass becomes a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges DAMP LAWNS.
explanation.definitionFit: A quagmire is soft boggy ground, and marshy terrain is exactly that, a synonym.

clue.text: Heartless men regularly turn in wizards

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is taken away

parts.note: males are men

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Cruel men repeatedly become sorcerers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes L from MALES; 'regularly' takes T, R, I from 'turn in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wizards can be experts or virtuosos, and maestros are masters of an art, especially music.

clue.text: Removes nuts from broken tureens!

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes nuts out of smashed soup bowls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like food but is slang for testicles; 'broken' rearranges TUREENS.
explanation.definitionFit: To castrate an animal is to take its testicles, slang nuts, so the definition is a jokey synonym.

clue.text: Creation of place to study poetry

parts.note: uni is short for university, a place to study
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: The founding of a school for studying poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creation' looks like a founding but means everything that exists.
explanation.definitionFit: Creation can mean all that was made, the whole cosmos, a synonym.

clue.text: Trending Roman sex god's close to brothel

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, written VI in Roman numerals
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A popular story about a Roman god of love and a bordello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex' is the Latin word for six, which Romans wrote VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Content spreading fast online, widely shared, is said to go viral, so it is trending.

clue.text: Ease of king touring American city

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the king surrounds the city

parts.note: rex is Latin for king
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: The comfort of a monarch on a tour of an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to loosen or unwind, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Stand next to soldiers?

parts.note: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg, and the egg sits on a little stand beside them

explanation.surface: An order to take position beside troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldiers' are British breakfast toast fingers, not troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The small holder for a boiled egg is a stand set beside the toast fingers at breakfast.

clue.text: Loudly made fun of Sherpa?

indicators.note: loudly means said out loud, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: guyed means mocked or ridiculed

explanation.surface: A mountain porter was openly mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Sherpa as an example: Sherpas lead Himalayan climbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sherpa is a Himalayan mountaineer who leads climbing parties, an example of one who leads the way.

clue.text: Small lamp in aircraft

parts.note: micro means very small
a lamp is a light

explanation.surface: A tiny lamp is fitted on a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A very light one- or two-seat powered plane is a kind of aircraft, an example.

clue.text: News report of small child cycling

indicators.note: cycling means the front letter goes round to the back

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A news story about a little child on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' looks like riding a bike but moves the M of MITE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A short piece in a newspaper or bulletin is a news item, a synonym.

clue.text: Happy to eat soft chocolate bar

indicators.note: to eat means to take in, so the happy word surrounds the soft one

parts.note: gay in its older sense means happy
lax means slack or soft

explanation.surface: Pleased to tuck into a soft candy.
explanation.walkthrough: Galaxy is a British brand of milk chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: Galaxy is a brand of milk chocolate bar sold in Britain, so it is an example.

clue.text: Walkers and motorcyclists heading off after hours

indicators.note: after puts the beheaded riders behind the hours letter
heading off means the first letter goes

parts.note: bikers are motorcyclists

explanation.surface: Pedestrians and motorbike riders set out once the day's hours are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like departing but removes the B of BIKERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hikers are people who go on long walks in the country, so they are walkers.
